summary.text: Kathryn Lewandowsky is the Democratic candidate for the Washington House of Representatives, District 39-Position 1, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Sam Low (R).
A registered nurse, she has been involved in advocacy for single-payer healthcare and previously ran for the Washington State Senate in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Kathryn Lewandowsky was born on March 1, 1959, in Tacoma, Washington.
She earned an associate degree from Tacoma Community College in 1991 and a bachelor's degree from Western Washington University in 2017.
She has worked as a registered nurse and in banking, according to Ballotpedia.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, Lewandowsky said she had been a registered nurse in Washington for 40 years, had lived in Arlington since 2008, and had served as a union local unit chair, grievance officer and negotiating team member.
She said she had worked for Medicare for All since 2017 with the grassroots organization Whole Washington and nationally with One Payer States.
Ballotpedia lists her as affiliated with Whole Washington, One Payer States and Back Country Horsemen of Washington.
Lewandowsky lost to incumbent Keith Wagoner in the November 3, 2020 general election for Washington State Senate District 39.
She was eliminated in primaries for House District 39-Position 2 in 2022 and District 39-Position 1 in 2024, and advanced from the August 4, 2026 primary against Sam Low.
